intake.businessDescription: Shared temperature-controlled micro-fulfillment lockers and route-consolidation software for independent specialty food producers and local farms delivering into dense urban neighborhoods without owning refrigerated fleets.
intake.intendedCustomers: Independent specialty food makers, regional dairies, and artisanal bakeries fulfilling 40–350 weekly wholesale and direct-to-consumer cold orders.
intake.mainObjective: Validate unit economics with 12 paying anchor producers across 2 urban microhubs within 6 months.

ideaAnalysis.coreValueProposition: Eliminates refrigerated fleet CapEx for small specialty producers by combining shared urban cold-storage microhubs with automated multi-vendor route consolidation.
suppliedFactsSummary: Target launch corridor is Portland and Seattle metro areas.
Initial budget constraint is $85,000 at Pre-Seed / Validation stage.
Target customer volume is 40–350 weekly cold orders per producer.
6-month goal is 12 paying anchor producers across 2 microhubs.
Proposed pricing model: $350/month platform & cold-slot retainer plus $4.50 per consolidated tote delivered.

targetMarketAssumptions.statement: Independent food producers currently overpay for LTL refrigerated carriers or lose margin running half-empty personal vans.
targetMarketAssumptions.rationale: Standard industry friction for sub-pallet cold-chain shippers, though exact per-drop cost must be verified in discovery interviews.

targetMarketAssumptions.statement: Dense urban neighborhoods contain underutilized commercial kitchen or retail back-of-house square footage suitable for sub-leasing cold lockers.
targetMarketAssumptions.rationale: Requires landlord/partner validation before committing hardware capital.

potentialCustomerProblems.statement: Temperature excursions during last-mile handoffs cause spoilage and retail chargebacks.
Minimum order thresholds on third-party cold distributors lock out emerging regional brands.

missingInformation: Binding per-stop and per-route rates from regional refrigerated courier contractors.
Exact monthly sub-lease rate per commissary walk-in bay in Portland and Seattle.
Food safety permit scope for multi-tenant cold staging at host commissaries.

clarificationQuestions.question: Will Meridian employ its own last-mile drivers or partner with existing local courier fleets for hub-to-buyer delivery?
clarificationQuestions.whyItMatters: Determines fixed labor liability, commercial insurance needs, and how far $85,000 extends.
clarificationQuestions.answer: Partner with 2 regional refrigerated courier contractors for hub-to-store runs while producers drop off at the consolidated intake dock.

clarificationQuestions.question: What pricing model do you intend to test first with the 12 anchor producers?
clarificationQuestions.whyItMatters: Recurring base subscriptions stabilize cash flow compared to pure per-tote transactional pricing.
clarificationQuestions.answer: $350/month platform & cold-slot retainer plus $4.50 per consolidated tote delivered.

clarificationQuestions.question: Do your target microhub spaces already hold food-grade cold storage permits, or will retrofitting be required?
clarificationQuestions.whyItMatters: Electrical upgrades and municipal food-facility permitting can delay launch by 8–16 weeks.
clarificationQuestions.answer: Targeting existing commissary kitchens with spare walk-in capacity to avoid new construction permits.

keyBusinessRisks.statement: Two-sided density risk: low producer volume per hub prevents profitable route consolidation.
keyBusinessRisks.rationale: Route economics break down below critical tote density per ZIP code.

keyBusinessRisks.statement: Capital burn risk if custom locker hardware is purchased before locking in anchor retainers.
keyBusinessRisks.rationale: Budget of $85,000 leaves minimal buffer for hardware write-offs.

executiveReport.strategicThesis: Meridian Cold-Chain Microhubs can unlock profitable sub-pallet urban cold distribution in the Pacific Northwest by pairing asset-light commissary sub-leases with contracted couriers and an unvalidated $350/mo + $4.50/tote consolidation model.
executiveReport.executiveSummary:
Meridian addresses a clear operational gap for independent specialty food producers shipping 40–350 weekly cold orders across Portland and Seattle. By leveraging existing commissary walk-in infrastructure rather than building new cold facilities, the venture aligns realistically with its $85,000 Pre-Seed budget.

The core strategic priority over the next 6 months is proving route-level contribution margin and reliable cold-chain compliance across 12 paying anchor producers. Securing anchor producer Letters of Intent and locking in contracted courier SLAs prior to signing hub sub-leases—and gating Seattle expansion on Portland profitability—will mitigate the primary two-sided density and capital burn risks.

criticalRisksAndAssumptions.statement: Two-sided hub density threshold requires at least 6 active producers per microhub.
Commissary sub-leasing avoids new food-facility permitting delays.
criticalRisksAndAssumptions.rationale: Requires verification of host permit scope for multi-tenant staging.

recommendedNextSteps.action: Obtain binding per-stop route quotes from 3 regional refrigerated couriers in Portland and Seattle.
Close 6 conditional producer pilot LOIs at the $350/mo + $4.50/tote price point.
Finalize commissary host agreement with clear morning dock windows and liability coverage.
Execute 5 dry-run cold-chain validation routes with Bluetooth loggers prior to paid launch.
